topic: 2026 HHS Federal Poverty Guidelines (48 contiguous states + DC) and Texas SNAP eligibility/benefit parameters (FY2026 and FY2027)
verification_notes: Independent re-check on 2026-09-26; every numeric value re-confirmed against the official source, no mismatches found, no values changed. HHS 2026 guidelines (sizes 1-8, +$5,680) and FR doc 2026-00755 (Jan 15, 2026) confirmed on ASPE page. SNAP FY2026 income limits (130/100/165%), allotments sizes 1-8 + $218 each additional, $24 minimum, standard deductions $209/$209/$223/$261/$299, shelter cap $744, homeless $198.99, assets $3,000/$4,500, change-reporting $125 confirmed from the USDA FY2026 COLA memo PDF (signed Aug 14, 2025). FY2026 sizes 9-10 income limits and C-121.1 Texas figures (SME $170, SUA $445, BUA $400, telephone $62, Rev. 25-4 eff. Oct 1, 2025) confirmed on Texas Works Handbook C-120 page; sizes 9-10 allotments ($2,007/$2,225) confirmed on C-1431 allotment chart PDF. SNAP FY2027 values (all income limits, allotments incl. 9-17 +$225 and 18+ $3,887 cap, $25 minimum, standard deductions $217/$217/$229/$268/$308, shelter $769, homeless $205.66, assets $3,000/$4,750, change-reporting $150) confirmed from the USDA FY2027 COLA memo PDF dated Aug 21, 2026. 20% earned income deduction (A-1425.1) and $35 medical threshold (A-1428) confirmed in Texas Works Handbook. $5,000 resource limit (A-1220, Rev. 15-4), B-471 (Rev. 15-4)/B-472 (Rev. 26-1) cat-el rules, and A-1238.5 vehicle thresholds $1,500/$8,700/$22,500 (Rev. 24-2) confirmed. FNS eligibility page confirms elderly/disabled households only need to meet the net income limit. Removed unconfirmed note about ASPE price-change wording. USDA/FNS pages return 403 to automated fetch; memo PDFs were read via browser same-origin fetch. Not independently re-confirmed: claim that no Texas Works Handbook 26-4 revision had posted (revisions index URL returned 404).
effective_period: HHS 2026 poverty guidelines (published Jan 2026); SNAP FY2026 = Oct 1, 2025 - Sep 30, 2026; SNAP FY2027 = Oct 1, 2026 - Sep 30, 2027

snap_FY2026.applies_to: 48 States, D.C., Guam, Virgin Islands (income standards); 48 States and D.C. (allotments/deductions); confirmed identical in Texas Works Handbook C-121 (Rev. 25-4, eff. Oct. 1, 2025)

texas_specific_FY2026.source: Texas Works Handbook C-121.1 (Rev. 25-4, eff. Oct. 1, 2025)

snap_FY2027.source: USDA FNA memo 'SNAP - Fiscal Year 2027 Cost-of-Living Adjustments' dated August 21, 2026
snap_FY2027.applies_to: 48 States, D.C., Guam, Virgin Islands (income standards); 48 States and D.C. (allotments/deductions). Texas Works Handbook had not yet posted an Oct 2026 (26-4) revision as of 2026-09-26.

texas_bbce.gross_income_limit: 165% of FPIL (TANF Non-cash categorical eligibility); dollar amounts = gross_monthly_income_limit_165pct column above
texas_bbce.rule: Household is categorically eligible if all members are approved for TANF cash or SSI, or the household meets the resource criteria for TANF Non-cash (combined $5,000 limit for liquid assets and excess vehicle value) and has gross income <= 165% FPIL. TANF-NC categorically eligible households are not subject to the resource or gross and net income limits (B-472, Rev. 26-1).
texas_bbce.source: Texas Works Handbook B-471 (Rev. 15-4), B-472 (Rev. 26-1), C-121 footnote

texas_snap_asset_rules.rule_text: A household is not eligible for benefits if the total value of countable resources (liquid resources and excess vehicle value) is over $5,000 (A-1220, Rev. 15-4).

vehicles.source: Texas Works Handbook A-1238 (Rev. 24-2, eff. April 1, 2024)

notes: All figures copied from official sources; none estimated. FY2026 SNAP limits are based on 2025 poverty guidelines; FY2027 SNAP limits (Oct 1, 2026) are based on the 2026 HHS guidelines (net 100% for 1 person = $15,960/12 = $1,330). FY2026 sizes 9-10 come from Texas Works Handbook C-121/C-1431; FY2027 USDA memo lists sizes 1-8 plus each-additional only. FY2027 Texas-specific utility allowances (SUA/BUA/telephone/SME) not yet published in the Texas Works Handbook as of 2026-09-26 (latest revision 26-3, July 2026). Texas uses BBCE with a 165% FPIL gross limit and a $5,000 resource limit, so the federal $3,000/$4,500 ($4,750 in FY2027) asset limits generally do not bind in Texas. Households with an elderly/disabled member need only meet the net income test (FNS). The FY2027 USDA memo PDF was blocked for automated fetch (403) and was read via an in-app browser.
